verses.1: Of David. Contend, O LORD, with those contending against me; fight against those warring with me.
verses.2: Take up a shield and buckler and rise up to my aid.
verses.3: Draw the sword and bar the way against those pursuing me. Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”
verses.4: Let those seeking my life be put to shame and caught in their guilt; let those plotting evil against me turn back and be disgraced.
verses.5: Let them be like chaff before the wind, and may the angel of the LORD drive them away.
verses.6: Let their path be darkness and stumbling, and may the angel of the LORD pursue them.
verses.7: For they have secretly plotted my ruin, and in vain they have dug a trap for my life.
verses.8: Let deception come to them, a snare they did not know; let the trap they set ensnare them. In their own snare may they fall.
verses.9: And my soul will rejoice in the LORD; my heart will exult in his salvation.
verses.10: All my bones will say: “O LORD, who is like you, saving the poor from the strong and the poor and needy from the one who robs them?”
verses.11: False witnesses rise up, who do not know me, and they question me.
verses.12: They repay me evil for good, and they strip my soul bare.
verses.13: But as for me, when they grieved me, I wore sackcloth; I afflicted my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned to my bosom.
verses.14: I walked as one mourning a brother, as one who mourns like a mother, I grieved.
verses.15: And when I was weak, they rejoiced, and they gathered, and they attacked me—wicked men who did not know me, they tore and did not heal.
verses.16: They mocked me with their taunts, they gnashed their teeth at me.
verses.17: O LORD, how long will you look on? Rescue my soul from their destruction, my only one from the lions.
verses.18: I will praise you in a great assembly, I will laud you among a mighty people.
verses.19: Let not my foes rejoice over me in vain, let not my haters wink their eyes.
verses.20: For they speak to me words of peace, but they devise plots of deceit.
verses.21: They opened wide their mouths against me, saying, “Aha, aha! We have seen it with our eyes.”
verses.22: You, O LORD, have seen; do not be silent. O Lord, do not be far from me.
verses.23: Wake up, and rouse yourself for my cause. O my God, my Lord, for my right.
verses.24: Judge me, O LORD, according to your justice, O LORD my God, and let them not rejoice over me.
verses.25: Let them not say in their hearts, “Aha, our hearts desire it!” Let them not say, “We have devoured him!”
verses.26: Let them be put to shame together, those who rejoice at my misfortune. Let those who boast against me be clothed in disgrace and dishonor.
verses.27: Let those who delight in my righteousness rejoice and be glad, and let them always say, “Great is the LORD, who delights in the peace of his servant.”
verses.28: And my tongue will meditate on your justice; all the day your praise.

notes:
Notes
- v. 13: "my prayer returned to my bosom" — the Hebrew phrase תָּשֽׁוּב לְחֵיקִי is metaphorical, indicating that the psalmist's prayer was turned inward, perhaps in sorrow or frustration.
- v. 17: "my only one from the lions" — the Hebrew uses “ יחִידָתִי” which is typically feminine, but here used metaphorically for the psalmist's life or soul. Rendered as "my only one" to preserve the metaphor.
- v. 21: "Aha, aha! We have seen it with our eyes." — the doubling of "Aha!" (הֶאָח) in the Hebrew is rendered to reflect its forceful repetition.
- v. 27: "who delights in the peace of his servant" — the Hebrew is ambiguous between "delights in" and "delights to see." The former is chosen for clarity and stylistic consistency.

[2] Take up a shield and buckler and rise up to my aid.

[3] Draw the sword and bar the way against those pursuing me. Say to my soul, “I am your salvation.”

[4] Let those seeking my life be put to shame and caught in their guilt; let those plotting evil against me turn back and be disgraced.

[5] Let them be like chaff before the wind, and may the angel of the LORD drive them away.

[6] Let their path be darkness and stumbling, and may the angel of the LORD pursue them.

[7] For they have secretly plotted my ruin, and in vain they have dug a trap for my life.

[8] Let deception come to them, a snare they did not know; let the trap they set ensnare them. In their own snare may they fall.

[9] And my soul will rejoice in the LORD; my heart will exult in his salvation.

[10] All my bones will say: “O LORD, who is like you, saving the poor from the strong and the poor and needy from the one who robs them?”

[11] False witnesses rise up, who do not know me, and they question me.

[12] They repay me evil for good, and they strip my soul bare.

[13] But as for me, when they grieved me, I wore sackcloth; I afflicted my soul with fasting, and my prayer returned to my bosom.

[14] I walked as one mourning a brother, as one who mourns like a mother, I grieved.

[15] And when I was weak, they rejoiced, and they gathered, and they attacked me—wicked men who did not know me, they tore and did not heal.

[16] They mocked me with their taunts, they gnashed their teeth at me.

[17] O LORD, how long will you look on? Rescue my soul from their destruction, my only one from the lions.

[18] I will praise you in a great assembly, I will laud you among a mighty people.

[19] Let not my foes rejoice over me in vain, let not my haters wink their eyes.

[20] For they speak to me words of peace, but they devise plots of deceit.

[21] They opened wide their mouths against me, saying, “Aha, aha! We have seen it with our eyes.”

[22] You, O LORD, have seen; do not be silent. O Lord, do not be far from me.

[23] Wake up, and rouse yourself for my cause. O my God, my Lord, for my right.

[24] Judge me, O LORD, according to your justice, O LORD my God, and let them not rejoice over me.

[25] Let them not say in their hearts, “Aha, our hearts desire it!” Let them not say, “We have devoured him!”

[27] Let those who delight in my righteousness rejoice and be glad, and let them always say, “Great is the LORD, who delights in the peace of his servant.”

[28] And my tongue will meditate on your justice; all the day your praise.

Notes
- v. 13: "my prayer returned to my bosom" — the Hebrew phrase תָּשֽׁוּב לְחֵיקִי is metaphorical, indicating that the psalmist's prayer was turned inward, perhaps in sorrow or frustration.
- v. 17: "my only one from the lions" — the Hebrew uses “ יחִידָתִי” which is typically feminine, but here used metaphorically for the psalmist's life or soul. Rendered as "my only one" to preserve the metaphor.
- v. 21: "Aha, aha! We have seen it with our eyes." — the doubling of "Aha!" (הֶאָח) in the Hebrew is rendered to reflect its forceful repetition.
- v. 27: "who delights in the peace of his servant" — the Hebrew is ambiguous between "delights in" and "delights to see." The former is chosen for clarity and stylistic consistency.
